skill.name: plate-handler
skill.description: Build Plate.js rich text editors for React applications, including simple comment editors and detailed document editors.
skill.summary: Guides implementation of Plate.js editors with shadcn UI components, plugin choices, toolbars, and state handling.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

content.value_statement: React teams need rich text editors that match their design system. This skill guides Plate.js setup, plugins, toolbars, and state handling.
actual_capabilities: Choose between simple comment editors and detailed document editors.
Provide shadcn CLI commands for installing Plate editor components.
Recommend component paths for simple and detailed editor implementations.
Configure Plate plugins for marks, headings, blockquotes, and toolbars.
Use value and onChange patterns for editor state management.
Reference example implementations for small and detailed editors.
limitations: Requires a React project that can use Plate.js and shadcn UI.
Does not implement backend persistence, access control, or file uploads.
Package names and shadcn commands may change across Plate.js versions.
Does not provide full sanitization logic for rendering stored HTML.

use_cases.title: Add comment formatting
use_cases.description: Create a compact editor with bold, italic, underline, and minimal toolbar controls.

use_cases.title: Build a blog editor
use_cases.description: Create a detailed editor with headings, blockquotes, marks, and a fixed toolbar.

use_cases.title: Standardize editor setup
use_cases.description: Give teams a repeatable Plate.js setup path with shared components and state patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple editor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for comments or short text fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to build a simple Plate.js editor for comments. Include basic marks and a compact toolbar.

prompt_templates.title: Add a detailed editor
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for documents or blog posts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to create a detailed Plate.js editor. Include headings, blockquote, marks, and a fixed toolbar.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate editor state
prompt_templates.scenario: State handling for forms and drafts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to connect Plate.js value changes to my form state. Keep the editor reusable and typed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a full editor system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for shared product components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to design simple and detailed Plate.js editors for our app. Include paths, plugins, toolbar groups, and persistence notes.

output_examples.input: I need a small editor for chat messages.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use the simple editor path. Include bold, italic, underline, and a compact toolbar. Store changes through value and onChange.

output_examples.input: I need a blog post editor with headings and quotes.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use the detailed editor path. Add heading plugins, blockquote support, mark buttons, and a fixed toolbar.

output_examples.input: I want consistent Plate.js setup across the app.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: install shared Plate UI components first. Then create reusable simple and detailed editor components in one folder.

best_practices: Confirm package installation commands before running them in a project.
Keep simple editors minimal and reserve complex plugins for document editing.
Store Plate values through controlled state or form state, then sanitize rendered output.
anti_patterns: Running latest package commands without reviewing generated file changes.
Using a full document editor for short chat or comment fields.
Rendering stored rich text with raw HTML without a sanitization plan.

faq.question: What does this skill build?
faq.answer: It guides Plate.js rich text editor setup for React projects using shadcn UI components.

faq.question: Can it create both simple and detailed editors?
faq.answer: Yes. It separates compact comment editors from detailed document or CMS editors.

faq.question: Does it require shadcn UI?
faq.answer: The guidance expects shadcn UI components for editor surfaces, toolbars, and generated component files.

faq.question: Does it store editor content?
faq.answer: It explains value and onChange patterns, but storage implementation remains part of the host app.

faq.question: Does it cover secure HTML rendering?
faq.answer: It warns against unsafe raw HTML rendering and recommends Plate serialization when read-only HTML is needed.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
